title: The legend of Vishvamitra, continued
introduction: Vashishta offers hospitality to Vishvamitra and his armies. Even though the King Vishvamitra is disinclined to pressurise a hermit with such a burdensome affair of hospitality to hosts, Vashishta entreats the king to accept. Vishvamitra had to oblige the same. Vashishta summons his do-all Divine Sacred Cow, Shabala, also known as Kaamadhenu, requests her to generate heaps of tasteful foodstuffs for a royal banquet as well as for military rations.
closing: The reverential greeting namaste is from the root nam 'bend down a little...' before upper echelons and the word namas is usually translated a 'salutation by bending a little...' and namas kāra is the act of doing so. This word namaḥ= na aham is 'not me...' te astu but 'you, it shall be...' rather, 'I have lost my 'I-ness' before you as I am humbling myself to your high knowledge or, high seat, or elder age...' and let your 'your-ness' prevail over me, for I am somewhat an inferior being before you...' is the latent meaning.
This is either vocalised or coupled with the gesture of adjoining palms, and that mudra 'gesture...' is called an~jali or as a Latinian friend of ours has provided its Latin counterpart as:

The infinitive is iungere manus ante pectus 'to join hands in front of your chest...' or merely iungere manus 'to join hands...' We can say iungimus manus ante pectus 'we join or fold our hands in front of us...' iungo manus ante pectus 'I fold my hands...' iungite manus ante pectus 'fold your hands in front of you...' This last sentence is the - you, plural - is in command form. Again, you may leave out ante pectus for succinctness.

And if the word iun with a half 'n' nasal is matched with Sanskrit añ in an~jali and the word ngo is matched with Sanskrit ñja as the English 'g' is most often used for Sanskrit 'ja' by Max Muller et al., the two an~jali of Sanskrit and iungo Latin have same pronunciation and portent in prayer or traditional salutation.
Thus, this is the 52nd chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
तं दृष्ट्वा परमप्रीतो विश्वामित्रो महाबलः |
प्रणतो विनयाद्वीरो वसिष्ठं जपतां वरम्
verses.iast:
tam dṛṣṭvā parama prīto viśvāmitro mahābalaḥ |
praṇato vinayāt vīro vasiṣṭham japatām varam
verses.translation: On seeing at that best sage among best meditators Sage Vashishta, the great-mighty and valorous Vishvamitra is highly rejoiced and obediently made an obeisance to the sage.

glosses.meaning: [who is] among meditators, the best sage

verses.devanagari:
स्वागतं तव चेत्युक्तो वसिष्ठेन महात्मना |
आसनं चास्य भगवान् वसिष्ठो व्यादिदेश ह
verses.iast:
svāgatam tava ca iti ukto vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā |
āsanam ca asya bhagavān vasiṣṭho vyādideśa ha
verses.translation: The great-souled Vashishta spoke, "you are welcome," and that godly sage has indeed shown a high seat to Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: thus, by great-souled, Vashishta, is spoken to [Vishvamitra]
to him [to Vishvamitra, ] seat, also, ordering [showing,] indeed.

verses.devanagari:
उपविष्टाय च तदा विश्वामित्राय धीमते |
यथान्यायं मुनिवरः फलमूलमुपाहरत्
verses.iast:
upaviṣṭāya ca tadā viśvāmitrāya dhīmate |
yathā nyāyam muni varaḥ phala mūlam upāharat
verses.translation: The eminent saint Vashishta then customarily offered fruits and tuber to the courageous Vishvamitra who by now has assumed a seat.

glosses.meaning: to one who is sitting, courageous one, to Vishvamitra

verses.devanagari:
प्रतिगृह्य तु तां पूजां वसिष्ठाद्राजसत्तमः |
तपोऽग्निहोत्रशिष्येषु कुशलं पर्यपृच्छत
विश्वामित्रो महातेजा वनस्पतिगणे तथा |
सर्वत्र कुशलं चाह वसिष्ठो राजसत्तमः
verses.iast:
pratigṛhya tu tām pūjām vasiṣṭhāt rāja sattamaḥ |
tapo agni hotra śiṣyeṣu kuśalam paryapṛcchata
viśvāmitro mahātejā vanaspati gaṇe tathā |
sarvatra kuśalam ca āha vasiṣṭho rāja sattamam
verses.translation: On receiving that deference from Vashishta, then that unsurpassed king Vishvamitra asked after the well-being of the ascesis, Fire-rituals and disciples and their progress in that hermitage, and that great-resplendent Vishvamitra has also asked after the well being of flora and fauna of the hermitage, and Vashishta reported to the matchless king about the all round well-being of every activity.

glosses.meaning: regarding trees, clumps of - of flora and implied fauna of hermitage
to king, the matchless, said - reported.

verses.devanagari:
सुखोपविष्टं राजानं विश्वामित्रं महातपाः |
पप्रच्छ जपतां श्रेष्ठो वसिष्ठो ब्रह्मणः सुतः
verses.iast:
sukha upaviṣṭam rājānam viśvāmitram mahātapāḥ |
papraccha japatām śreṣṭho vasiṣṭho brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ
verses.translation: Vashishta the supreme one among meditators, a great-ascetic, and the brainchild of Brahma has then asked Vishvamitra who is sitting at ease.

verses.devanagari:
कच्चित्ते कुशलं राजन् कच्चिद्धर्मेण रंजयन् |
प्रजाः पालयसे राजन् राजवृत्तेन धार्मिक
verses.iast:
kaccit te kuśalam rājan kaccit dharmeṇa rañjayan |
prajāḥ pālayase rājan rāja vṛttena dhārmika
verses.translation: " 'I hope that you are fine! And oh, righteous king, hope that you are ruling people righteously with kingly righteousness to their contentment.
notes: The kingly righteousness is one component among the four primary concerns of the kingcraft as said at: nyāyena ārjanam arthasya varthanam pālanam tathā | sat pātre pratipattiḥ ca rāja vṛttam catur vidham || 'monies are to be earned righteously, they are to be enriched righteously, and safeguarded righteously, and they are to be endowed to righteous deeds or persons, for welfare of the state, righteously...'

glosses.meaning: to you, well-being, I hope - All is well!
people, righteously, while satisfying to their contentment

verses.devanagari:
कच्चित्ते सुभृता भृत्याः कच्चित्तिष्ठन्ति शासने |
कच्चित्ते विजिताः सर्वे रिपवो रिपुसूदन
verses.iast:
kaccit te subhṛtā bhṛtyāḥ kaccit tiṣṭhanti śāsane |
kaccit te vijitāḥ sarve ripavo ripu sūdana
verses.translation: " 'I hope your servants are looked after well, hope all of them are abiding by the rulership, oh, vanquisher of adversaries, I hope that you have surely vanquished all of your adversaries.

glosses.meaning: well-served - are they looked after well, I hope

verses.devanagari:
कच्चित् बले च कोशे च मित्रेषु च परंतप |
कुशलं ते नरव्याघ्र पुत्रपौत्रे तथानघ
verses.iast:
kaccit bale ca kośe ca mitreṣu ca parantapa |
kuśalam te nara vyāghra putra pautre tathā anagha
verses.translation: " 'For you are an impeccable one and an emery-inflamer, oh, tigerly-man, I hope that your forces, exchequer and confederates are fine, and all is well with your sons and grandsons." Thus Vashishta asked the well-being of Vishvamitra.

glosses.itrans: bale ca koshe ca mitreSu ca
glosses.iast: bale ca kośe ca mitreṣu ca
glosses.devanagari: बले च कोशे च मित्रेषु च
glosses.meaning: in forces, and, in exchequer, and, among friends [confederates,] also

verses.devanagari:
सर्वत्र कुशलं राजा वसिष्ठं प्रत्युदाहरत् |
विश्वामित्रो महातेजा वसिष्ठं विनयान्वितम्
verses.iast:
sarvatra kuśalam rājā vasiṣṭham pratyudāharat |
viśvāmitro mahātejā vasiṣṭham vinaya anvitam
verses.translation: "The great-resplendent king Vishvamitra respectfully replied Sage Vashishta saying, 'everything is fine.'

verses.devanagari:
कृत्वा तौ सुचिरं कालं धर्मिष्ठौ ताः कथास्तदा |
मुदा परमया युक्तौ प्रीयेतां तौ परस्परम्
verses.iast:
kṛtvā tau suciram kālam dharmiṣṭhau tāḥ kathāḥ tadā |
mudā paramayā yuktau prīyetām tau parasparam
verses.translation: "Both of those celebrities of conscientious then exchanged pleasantries for a long time with their rejoice heightening and gladdening one another.

verses.devanagari:
ततो वसिष्ठो भगवान् कथान्ते रघुनंदन |
विश्वामित्रमिदं वाक्यमुवाच प्रहसन्निव
verses.iast:
tato vasiṣṭho bhagavān kathā ante raghunandana |
viśvāmitram idam vākyam uvāca prahasan iva
verses.translation: "Then at the end of discussions, oh, Rama the legatee of Raghu, that godly Sage Vashishta smilingly spoke this sentence to Vishvamitra.

verses.devanagari:
आतिथ्यं कर्तुमिच्छामि बलस्यास्य महाबल |
तव चैवाप्रमेयस्य यथार्हं संप्रतीच्छ मे
verses.iast:
ātithyam kartum icchāmi balasya asya mahābala |
tava ca eva aprameyasya yathā arham sampratīccha me
verses.translation: " 'I wish to offer guestship befitting to your status, oh, great-forceful king Vishvamitra, to a matchless one like you and to this military force of yours, kindly accept it from me.

glosses.meaning: guestship, to do [to offer,] I wish to[ me = from me
well, in turn, you accede] = kindly accede to it.

verses.devanagari:
सत्क्रियां तु भवानेतां प्रतीच्छतु मया कृताम् |
राजंस्त्वमतिथिश्रेष्ठः पूजनीयः प्रयत्नतः
verses.iast:
sat.hkriyām tu bhavān etām pratīcchatu mayā kṛtām |
rājan tvam atithi śreṣṭhaḥ pūjanīyaḥ prayatnataḥ
verses.translation: " 'You may kindly accept all these hospitalities offered by me, oh king, for you are an important guest you ought to be reverenced effortfully.' So said Vashishta to Vishvamitra.
notes: 'It is quiet meaningless on the part of this sage, subsisting on wild fruits and tubers, to offer a royal banquet or rations to military and feed to horses and elephants' - is the thinking of King Vishvamitra. For that, the sage is saying that a king is to be reverenced 'effortfully...' But, Vishvamitra is reluctantly evading the so-called hospitality for 'royals' and 'armies' from a poor hermit.

glosses.meaning: all these, good, works [hospitalities,] on their part

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्तो वसिष्ठेन विश्वामित्रो महामतिः |
कृतमित्यब्रवीद्राजा पूजावाक्येन मे त्वया
verses.iast:
evam ukto vasiṣṭhena viśvāmitro mahāmatiḥ |
kṛtam iti abravīt rājā pūjā vākyena me tvayā
verses.translation: "When sage Vashishta said in this way, that highly-intellectual king Vishvamitra said to him, 'hospitality is deemed to have been offered to me with your reverential words, it is enough and nothing more is necessary.'

glosses.meaning: by Vashishta, thus, said - to the sage
done[hospitality is deemed to have been offered - and nothing more is required

verses.devanagari:
फलमूलेन भगवन्विद्यते यत्तवाश्रमे |
पाद्येनाचमनीयेन भगवद्दर्शनेन च
सर्वथा च महाप्राज्ञ पूजार्हेण सुपूजितः |
नमस्तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि मैत्रेणेक्षस्व चक्षुषा
verses.iast:
phala mūlena bhagavan vidyate yat tava āśrame |
pādyena ācamanīyena bhagavad dar.hśanena ca
sarvathā ca mahāprājña pūjā arheṇa supūjitaḥ |
namaste astu gamiṣyāmi maitreṇa īkṣasva cakṣuṣā
verses.translation: " 'I am entertained with whatever item that obtains in your hermitage, say fruits, tubers and water for feet-wash and to wet mouth. Why those petty items, I regaled just by seeing you, a godly sage like. Oh, highly noetic sage, by yourself you are a sage worthy to be reverenced by one and all, such as you are you alone have reverenced me. Now I wish to take leave, please accept my obeisance to you, and please look upon us with a friendlily regard.
notes: The reverential salutation namas te astu is discussed in the endnote.

glosses.meaning: by water for feet-wash, by water for wetting mouth
[by you who are] for reverence, worthy
to you, obeisance, let there be [ le it be accepted]
with a friendly, eye [regard,] you look upon [us.]

verses.devanagari:
एवं ब्रुवन्तं राजानं वसिष्ठः पुनरेव हि |
न्यमंत्रयत धर्मात्मा पुनः पुनरुदारधीः
verses.iast:
evam bruvantam rājānam vasiṣṭhaḥ punaḥ eva hi |
nyamantrayata dharmātmā punaḥ punaḥ udāra dhīḥ
verses.translation: Even if the king was speaking in this way obliquely to him, that virtue-souled and magnanimous sage Vashishta entreated the king repeatedly.

glosses.meaning: in this way, [obliquely] speaking, to king

verses.devanagari:
बाढमित्येव गाधेयो वसिष्ठं प्रत्युवाच ह |
यथा प्रियं भगवतस्तथास्तु मुनिसत्तम
verses.iast:
bāḍham iti eva gādheyo vasiṣṭham pratyuvāca ha |
yathā priyam bhagavataḥ tathā astu muni sattama
verses.translation: "Gaadhi's son Vishvamitra then replied the eminent saint Vashishta, "Agreed! As it pleases the godly sage. So be it!'

glosses.meaning: to godlike you, as to how, it will be pleasing

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्तस्तथा तेन वसिष्ठो जपतां वरः |
आजुहाव ततः प्रीतः कल्माषीं धूतकल्मषः
verses.iast:
evam uktaḥ tathā tena vasiṣṭho japatām varaḥ |
ājuhāva tataḥ prītaḥ kalmāṣīm dhūta kalmaṣaḥ
verses.translation: "When Vishvamitra said that way then Vashishta, the best one among meditators, and one whose blemishes are laved is gladdened, and started calling his speckled cow, namely Shabala, yclept Kaamadhenu.

glosses.meaning: thus, that way, by him [Vishvamitra,] who is said
one who is laved, of blemishes

verses.devanagari:
एह्येहि शबले क्षिप्रं शृणु चापि वचो मम |
सबलस्यास्य राजर्षेः कर्तुं व्यवसितोऽस्म्यहम् |
भोजनेन महार्हेण सत्कारं संविधत्स्व मे
verses.iast:
ehi ehi śabale kṣipram śṛṇu ca api vaco mama |
sabalasya asya rājarṣeḥ kartum vyavasito asmi aham |
bhojanena mahā arheṇa satkāram saṃvidhat.hsva me
verses.translation: " 'Come on, oh, Shabala! Come quickly and listen to my words. I prepared to accord hospitality with a highly delectable royal banquet to this kingly sage together with all his forces. You arrange it for me.

glosses.meaning: with highly, delectable, feast [with a royal banquet]
together with, [all] forces, his, to kingly-sage
hospitality, to do [to accord,] prepared, I am
for me, you arrange for it.

verses.devanagari:
यस्य यस्य यथाकामं षड्रसेष्वभिपूजितम् |
तत्सर्वं कामधुक् दिव्ये अभिवर्ष कृते मम
verses.iast:
yasya yasya yathā kāmam ṣaḍ raseṣu abhipūjitam |
tat sarvam kāma dhuk divye abhivarṣa kṛte mama
verses.translation: "Oh, Kaamadhenu, the Divine Cow, the Milker of All-Desires, for my sake you shower whatsoever foodstuff is savoured by whosoever according to one's own piquancy from each of the six savour, that too plentifully.
notes: The six tastes that shall comprise an Indian meal are: 1] caustic, 2] acidic, 3] sweetish, 4] salty, 5] un-sweetish [bitter,] and 6] alkaline.

glosses.meaning: owing to, me - for my sake

verses.devanagari:
रसेनान्नेन पानेन लेह्यचोष्येण संयुतम् |
अन्नानां निचयं सर्वं सृजस्व शबले त्वर
verses.iast:
rasena annena pānena lehya coṣyeṇa saṃyutam |
annānām nicayam sarvam sṛjasva śabale tvara
verses.translation: " 'Oh, Shabala, you create heaps of savourily foodstuffs comprised of masticable items like crunchy foods, drinkable items like soft-drinks, tasteable items like honey-like viscous dishes, squeezable items like pulpy fruits, and be quick.' " So said Sage Vashishta to that Sacred Cow, Kaamadhenu, and Vishvamitra continued his narration.

glosses.meaning: every kind of, foodstuffs, heaps of
